crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was small, her mother looked at each of her drawings, said nothing, and fed it to the stove. Something was wrong with everything she made, and no one would say what.
In the mansion, she sat beside only one girl at meals. Every Monday before the burn, that girl lifted the incinerator lid to save what others had thrown away. "Nothing burns without one last look."

One Monday at lunch in the dining hall, the girl spread a row of drawings along the table, drawings {WITCH_NAME} had sent down the garbage chute. "What's wrong with these?" she asked, and the whole table leaned in to look. She turned to {WITCH_NAME}. "I'll save every one you ever throw away—" Before the girl could finish or anyone could answer, {WITCH_NAME} vanished, leaving an empty chair.
Before that day's burn, she dropped her new pencil portrait of the girl down the chute in the shower room, then went down to wait by the furnace.

Just before three, the girl straightened from the furnace holding the portrait, and {WITCH_NAME} brought the lid down on her neck. She pulled the portrait from the girl's fingers and vanished with it into her own bed.
At three, free time ended. Prisoners crowding back along the cell corridor reached the incinerator room's only door seconds after the clang. The girl lay alone under the lid. No one had come out.

In the trial court, they ruled it an accident: the propped lid had fallen on her as she leaned in alone. Then a prisoner opened the girl's clenched fist and found a torn corner of a pencil portrait. Anyone who had been at lunch knew who had drawn it. The rest was nowhere in the room. The prisoners understood: it had been torn from her dying hand and carried out without passing anyone, straight into {WITCH_NAME}'s bed.
fields.epitaph: She never stayed to hear that nothing was wrong with them.
fields.epithet: The girl who feeds the fire drawings no one has looked at
execution: The execution stand raises a bed, its blanket one vast sheet of her own drawing paper. She lies strapped beneath it, tucked in to the chin, and above her hangs the sharpened point of a giant pencil.

The pencil comes down and hatches back and forth, pressing through the paper into her, harder with every stroke. It never settles on one spot. It shades every inch, as if hunting for a wrong it cannot find.
At last it lifts and hovers. The paper lies shaded grey over her still shape, torn where the point went in.

magic.name: Tucked Away
magic.text: She vanishes from wherever she is and reappears tucked into her own bed.
